name: Tetrapotassium pyrophosphate
description: Tetrapotassium pyrophosphate (CAS 7320-34-5 ), commonly abbreviated as TKPP and listed as E450(v) in food applications, is an inorganic potassium salt used across industrial and food-grade processes. It functions primarily as a chelating agent, buffering agent, and dispersant, enabling formulators to control pH, sequester metal ions, and stabilize complex systems in various environments. In food processing, TKPP acts as an emulsifying salt and moisture-retention agent in processed cheese, seafood, and cured meat products to maintain texture and quality during storage. Industrial cleaning and textile processing rely on it to sequester calcium and magnesium ions in hard water, improving detergent efficiency and ensuring dye uptake uniformity across fabrics. In water treatment formulations, it prevents scale formation and controls corrosion by binding interfering metal ions, protecting infrastructure and maintaining flow efficiency in industrial systems. Building and construction applications use TKPP as a dispersant in cementitious and ceramic systems, improving workability and pigment distribution for more consistent and durable finished materials. Tetrapotassium pyrophosphate is supplied as a white powder or granule. Food-grade material is available to FCC and E450(v) specifications, while technical-grade product serves industrial applications. Standard commercial concentrations are typically offered at ≥95% or ≥98% purity depending on grade, ensuring reliable performance for cleaning, ceramics, and specialized water treatment needs.
